item.title: Fly River provincial government commits K25m for El Niño drought relief
item.description: The Fly River Provincial Government has allocated K25 million from its internal budget to deliver emergency relief and maintain key supply lines across Western Province during the ongoing El Niño drought. The Provincial Inter-Agency Disaster Committee confirmed today that the funds represent an independent commitment from the provincial government rather than external donor support or corporate co
item.content:encoded:
The Fly River Provincial Government has allocated K25 million from its internal budget to deliver emergency relief and maintain key supply lines across Western Province during the ongoing El Niño drought.

The Provincial Inter-Agency Disaster Committee confirmed today that the funds represent an independent commitment from the provincial government rather than external donor support or corporate contributions from Ok Tedi Mining Limited [OTML].

The disaster response funding will target three operational priorities:

Under a strategic logistics framework directed by the committee, emergency relief supplies will be sourced directly from Port Moresby and transported via dedicated air and river charters through Aiambak and Tabubil.

Strategic stockpiles of essential food items and fuel will be maintained across regional hubs in Daru, Balimo, Kiunga, Ningerum, and Tabubil, with immediate distribution prioritized for North and Middle Fly.

The committee noted that pre-positioning supplies closer to vulnerable rural populations is designed to mitigate delivery delays, prevent local shortage-driven price spikes, and ensure supply continuity through the extended dry spell.

Chaired by the Provincial Administrator in his capacity as Disaster Controller, the Provincial Inter-Agency Disaster Committee includes representatives from the Department of Provincial and Local Level Government Affairs, OTML, and the Sustainable Development Program.

item.title: Trukai Industries donates over K100,00 to support Morobe Show infrastructure
item.description: Trukai Industries has presented K133,100 to the Morobe Show Committee to support this year’s Morobe Show. The presentation was made today at the Lae Showgrounds to committee president Hans Mehl.
item.content:encoded:
Trukai Industries has presented K133,100 to the Morobe Show Committee to support this year’s Morobe Show.

The presentation was made today at the Lae Showgrounds to committee president Hans Mehl.

Mehl said the support would help the committee continue improving facilities at the showgrounds.

A new toilet block has been built along the main roadside, with other improvements made around the agricultural area.

“Any sponsorship is very valuable in improving the grounds, the facilities and the event overall,” Mehl said.

He thanked Trukai for its long-standing partnership with the Morobe Show, saying the company supports the event through both its commercial and agricultural displays.

“We love Trukai. Trukai is our partner and has been our partner for so many years,” he said.

Mehl said the committee also wants to make the showgrounds more useful throughout the year.

Plans include installing lights around the oval for night sports and developing a larger pavilion for other community activities.

“We’re trying to see how can we fulfil that and make the showground a public place where many functions can happen,” Mehl said.

item.title: Trobriand communities face food and water shortages
item.description: The people of the Trobriand Islands in Kiriwina-Goodenough District are facing severe effects of the prolonged dry weather on their food gardens and water supplies. ‎‎As the dry spell ends its fifth month, reports from the Milne Bay island say water tanks and well waters around homes are empty, and families are forced to travel far in search of drinking water.‎‎
item.content:encoded:
The people of the Trobriand Islands in Kiriwina-Goodenough District are facing severe effects of the prolonged dry weather on their food gardens and water supplies.

‎‎As the dry spell ends its fifth month, reports from the Milne Bay island say water tanks and well waters around homes are empty, and families are forced to travel far in search of drinking water.‎‎

People along the coast of the main Trobriand islands are walking as far as one kilometer inland into the swampy areas, where they dig wells to find drinking water, while their garden crops struggle to survive in the parched soil.‎‎

Speaking to NBC News this morning from the Trobriand Islands, Mulosaida Ward Councilor, Yaguma Towowoda, said crops are dying fast and household water tanks are empty.

‎‎"The crops we have now are sweet potatoes, cassava and taros but they've all been damaged because of the drought. We have wells some kilometers away from the villages that we have dug to fetch water."‎‎

Councilor Towowoda said the Northern and Central part of the main island, as well as the atolls, are now at risk of running out of food and water as the dry weather intensifies.‎‎

He added that relief supplies are expected to arrive soon for communities in the Northern, Central and the Atolls through the office of the Member for Kiriwina Goodenough.

‎‎Meanwhile, Trobriand Islander and Livestock Advisor with the Department of Agriculture and Livestock in the Milne Bay Provincial Administration, Ropsy Taudiri, said he used his time during his compassionate leave on the island to help communities asses the conditions of their garden crops, and what he observed was concerning.‎‎

"According to observations, there are certain crops that are drought-tolerant, meaning they can still produce food despite the dry weather. The strongest drought tolerant crop is giant taro but it's now beginning to wilt in this weather," Tadiri said.

‎‎"The sun is too strong and the crops stopped growing. Yams are drought-tolerant crops, but if the drought persists in the months to come, our people will lose all their food crops."

item.title: Coffee delays put farmers at risk
item.description: Coffee farmers in the Highlands could face further disruption to their income as the movement of coffee to Lae for export remains stalled during one of the busiest periods of the season. Coffee from producing areas, including as far as Mt Hagen, is transported by road to Lae, where it is prepared and transferred into shipping containers for international markets.
item.content:encoded:
Coffee farmers in the Highlands could face further disruption to their income as the movement of coffee to Lae for export remains stalled during one of the busiest periods of the season.

Coffee from producing areas, including as far as Mt Hagen, is transported by road to Lae, where it is prepared and transferred into shipping containers for international markets.

The stoppage is affecting the chain between growers and overseas buyers, with exporters holding coffee at warehouses and wharves while inspections and export clearances remain affected.

Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry president John Byrne said the disruption could have consequences well beyond the port, affecting growers, buyers, transport operators, storage facilities and workers who depend on the coffee trade.

“It’s not just the exporter that is affected. It goes right back to the grower,” Byrne said.

The situation is developing during the busiest month of the coffee export season, according to the LCCI.

Exporters have reportedly slowed or stopped sending new coffee to Lae while the issue remains unresolved.

Coffee already packed in international shipping containers could also face additional costs if it has to be removed and transported back to the Highlands because of Lae’s humidity.

For farmers, delays in getting coffee from the Highlands to overseas markets could mean delays further along the payment and supply chain.

Byrne said the disruption also risks affecting Papua New Guinea’s reputation with international coffee buyers if orders cannot be fulfilled on time.

The export stoppage follows the transition from the former Coffee Industry Corporation to the National Coffee Authority, with administrative and financial authority issues affecting some operations, including export inspections and clearances.

LCCI is calling for the issue to be resolved quickly so coffee can continue moving from growers to international markets.

item.title: New facilities will transform learning at school, says principal
item.description: Students will now be able to do real science experiments in the fields of physics, biology and chemistry, says Mananda High School Principal John Wangi. Speaking during the opening of the four-in-one Science and Computer Laboratories last Friday, Wangi said the new high school and several other projects were commissioned on the same day.
item.content:encoded:
Students will now be able to do real science experiments in the fields of physics, biology and chemistry, says Mananda High School Principal John Wangi.

Speaking during the opening of the four-in-one Science and Computer Laboratories last Friday, Wangi said the new high school and several other projects were commissioned on the same day.

He said science and computer laboratories are essential components of modern education, transforming abstract academic concepts into tangible, hands-on learning experiences.

"Moving beyond theory-only instruction bridges the gap between understanding a concept and applying it in the real world," he said.

"On behalf of the school administration, the students and the community, I thank MRDC for the funding."

Wangi further thanked the National Energy Authority [NEA] for its Solar Electricity Project, stating that the school had faced serious problems without reliable power.

"When the grid failed, learning failed. Our laptops and computers could not work, our lab experiments were useless, and at night students could not study after 6pm," he said.

The principal also stressed that to add to these developments, the provision of free WiFi by Hides Gas Development Company [HGDC] is a game changer, connecting the rural community to the outside world.

"The Starlink connection has taken Mananda High School out of isolation and placed it on the map of digital learning," he said.

He also acknowledged ExxonMobil PNG for the new staff house that was also commissioned on the day.

A groundbreaking ceremony also took place for a four-in-one Social Science block. Wangi said the block will complete the classroom requirements for senior high school status.

Hela Provincial Government has funded the construction of a four-in-one administration block.

"The building will accommodate the school administration, general staffroom, conference room, reception desk, school bursar, staff toilet facilities and storerooms," Wangi said.

Present for the event were Hela Governor Philip Undialu, Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu, development partners and project developers.

item.title: Lae City launches digital platform for online land tax payments
item.description: Residents and business owners in Papua New Guinea's industrial hub can now pay land taxes online following the launch of a new digital portal by the Lae City Authority [LCA]. The platform, known as ServiceLink, was officially launched on Monday in partnership with fintech company NiuPay to digitize municipal services and reduce severe counter congestion at city offices.
item.content:encoded:
Residents and business owners in Papua New Guinea's industrial hub can now pay land taxes online following the launch of a new digital portal by the Lae City Authority [LCA].

The platform, known as ServiceLink, was officially launched on Monday in partnership with fintech company NiuPay to digitize municipal services and reduce severe counter congestion at city offices.

Through the new system, ratepayers can register, link property records, and settle land tax bills remotely without carrying cash or waiting in physical queues.

Lae City Authority Chief Executive Officer Robin Calistus said the portal is designed to modernize administrative operations and streamline civic transactions.

"Basically, you are in the office or you are at home actually doing the transactions through the ServiceLink that is being provided," Calistus said.

"We want them to just stay in the office and do the payment."

NiuPay Chief Operating Officer Trevor Manokore said the digital platform directly addresses safety and efficiency concerns surrounding cash handling in the city.

"The elimination of cash payments is a big one," Manokore said. "People no longer have to carry cash around."

While land tax collection is the first function integrated into ServiceLink, municipal authorities plan to phase in additional digital services, including trading licenses and garbage management fees.

item.title: Kerevat National School of Excellence commissions new smart classrooms
item.description: 12 new smart classrooms and an auditorium were commissioned at the Kerevat National School of Excellence in East New Britain last Friday. Education Minister Francis Siune and Secretary for Education Dr. Uke Kombra travelled to Kerevat to officiate at the ceremony.
item.content:encoded:
12 new smart classrooms and an auditorium were commissioned at the Kerevat National School of Excellence in East New Britain last Friday.

Education Minister Francis Siune and Secretary for Education Dr. Uke Kombra travelled to Kerevat to officiate at the ceremony.

The commissioning marks a major milestone for one of the country's six National Schools of Excellence under the Science, technology, Engineering and Mathematics [STEM] program.

The new facilities include 12 fully equipped smart classrooms fitted with smart boards and internet connectivity, and an auditorium.

The buildings, costing more than K3 million, were co-funded by the National Government through the Department of Education and the school’s administration.

Minister Siune said this is part of the Government's commitment to improve the quality of education in the country.

"The world is changing quickly and our children must be ready to meet those changes. We have to make sure our graduates are equipped with the knowledge, skills and confidence they need."

Kerevat School of Excellence, formally known as Kerevat National High School, is located in the Gazelle District. It is one of the four Schools of Excellence that have existed since colonial days.

Selected students from around the country attend the school to complete their Grades 11 and 12.

Previously, the school was known for all the wrong reasons, including reports of cult activities, deteriorating infrastructure and alleged misuse of funds that left it on the brink of collapse.

The school was temporarily closed in 2011 but was reopened a year later.

The current school principal Paul Kupi said Kerevat has moved from strength to strength over the years to restore its glory days.

"I would like to challenge our division and everyone to work together to improve performance. I challenge all of us to use these facilities to change the mindset of our students so we can produce better young Papua New Guineans."

The new infrastructure is expected to enhance teaching and learning, improve student performance, and put Kerevat as a model school for smart learning in the country.

item.title: Madang Jack’s branch relocates shop
item.description: Jack's of PNG has moved its Madang shop to a new location as of Saturday last week. The shop was relocated to the town's Central Business District within the old National Development Bank building, along Kasagten Road.
item.content:encoded:
Jack's of PNG has moved its Madang shop to a new location as of Saturday last week.

The shop was relocated to the town's Central Business District within the old National Development Bank building, along Kasagten Road.

A small opening ceremony, which included a short Hindu ritual, was performed by the company's Business Development Manager, Yogesh Samy.

Samy said the ritual is a display of their Hindu belief about prosperity.

"That's our Hindu belief. So whenever we open a new shop, we do a Indian ritual. That's basically our Indian way before we start business. We have requested a priest to come but unfortunately he's caught up with other things and didn't come so I had to do this.

"The new shop is smaller than the previous but is a bonus for us. It's easier now for customers as the shop is located right in the heart of town and they can walk in any time. Before it was outside and only few people went," he said.

Samy added that the shop will soon be stocking up on new range of items for Christmas.

He assured customers that they would not be left disappointed when it comes to quality and design.

"Our products are all quality and are original PNG designs. We also cater for all age groups," he added.

Jack's of PNG currently has four shops in Port Moresby, and one each in Madang, Kokopo, Lae, and Mt. Hagen.

A second shop is expected to open soon in the Westen Highlands capital.

According to Samy, the company's future plans include extending to Alotau, Buka, and Goroka.

Basil Doro, Retail Manager in Madang, said the new location is more convenient for customers.

One of the first customers at the new shop was Robin Wike and his family soon after the entrance opened. Wike is a staff at Divine Word University and said he frequently visits Jack's because of quality and genuine prices.
